subject: Workplace Skills
title: Communicating Decisions Clearly
description: A quick win: understand Communicating Decisions Clearly.

hook.text: The CEO announced a new strategy. Three departments interpreted it differently. Execution fractured immediately.

buildup.text: A great decision poorly communicated becomes a bad decision. People act on what they understood, not what you meant.

discovery.text: Every decision communication needs three parts: what was decided, why, and what changes for the audience.

twist.text: Repetition isn't redundant. Tell the decision through multiple channels. If you communicate it once, 50% will miss it.

climax.text: After sharing a decision, ask: 'What questions do you have?' then 'Tell me what you heard.' Confirm understanding.

punchline.text: What, why, what changes. Say it three times, three ways.

quiz.question: What are the three essential parts of communicating a decision?
options: Who made it, when it takes effect, and who it impacts
What was decided, why it was decided, and what changes for the audience
The problem, the solution, and the expected timeline
